newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Safex backs financial market integration.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Safex backs financial market integration.

text.p: The South African Futures Exchange (Safex) said on Wednesday it supported the integration of the country's futures, stock and bond markets to the extent that it would improve efficiencies.

Stuart Rees, Safex's chief executive said closer co-operation should be achieved by creating an umbrella body with the three financial exchanges as operating subsidiaries, each retaining their independence and separate identity.
"(The envisaged structure) would be rather like any holding company...with the subsidiaries subordinate to the decisions of the board of directors of the holding company," Rees told Reuters.
The futures exchange said it had restructured internally to facilitate tighter links and urged that the process be concluded as swiftly as possible with minimal disruption.

Safex said in a statement the primary market function to be integrated was the margining system as it was essential that the risk between a position in either the bond and share market could be offset against an opposite position in derivatives.
It also supported integrated surveillance across the exchanges and closer clearing and trading system links.
Unnecessary or counterproductive competition between the markets should be avoided, but without losing the independent characters of the exchanges, Safex said.
The removal of exchange controls would result in increased foreign competition in local markets which was a more important focus than internal rivalry.

Rees said the idea of more integration between the markets had been in the back of market participants' minds for a long time and had again been discussed at a meeting of the executive council of South Africa's exchanges earlier this year.
"We realised that a lot of issues are cross market and arise continuously and the feeling of the council was that it was really time to consider integration," Rees said.
